item.tests: Tests clarification of an ambiguous target face and preservation of the unselected person.

answer_sheet.Which person to replace: The blonde woman on the right. Leave the bearded man on the left alone.
answer_sheet.Style: Keep it looking like the original beach photo; I want to be recognisable, so my hair can come with my face.
answer_sheet.Size and platform: Keep the original wide 16:9 framing; free-tier size is fine.

must_haves: Only the woman on the right receives the face from portrait-woman.jpg.
The bearded man on the left still looks like the same person (small drift from a redrawn photo is acceptable).
The woman on the right is recognisably the person in portrait-woman.jpg (her hair may come with the face), blended to the beach lighting and head angle.
The bodies, clothing, beach background and wide framing look the same at a glance.
changed: 2026-11-01: recognisable over untouched (user decision): the hair, and on video the clothes, may come with the new person; everything else stays

turns.text: Can you put my face from this park selfie onto someone in this beach photo? I thought it would be a fun picture to have, but I’m a little worried the swap might look out of place. To explain which person I mean, it’s the blonde woman on the right in the pic of two friends, not the bearded man on the left, who should stay exactly as he is. Please use my face from the portrait selfie, and my hair can come with it so I’m recognisable, while keeping it looking like the original beach photo. The original wide 16:9 framing should stay, and free-tier size is fine. Basically, just swap that one face and leave everything else alone, with no text or other edits.

dialog.agent:
I couldn't make your picture yet. Magic Hour refused the head swap because your account doesn't have enough credits. It costs 10 credits, nothing was made and nothing was charged.

**What I set up:**
- **Your photo:** your face and curly dark hair, so you're recognisable
- **Who changes:** only the blonde woman on the right
- **What stays:** the bearded man and everything else, with the same wide 16:9 framing, free-tier size and no text

**A risk to know first:** the head-swap tool can't be told which person to change. It may pick the right woman, but it could put your head on the man instead. A face swap can target just her using face detection, but it would only change her face, not her hair. So you'd look less like yourself.

**How you could go ahead:**
1. **Add credits and run the head swap.** This is the closest match to what you asked for. I'd check the result, and if it changed the wrong person, I'd fall back to a face swap aimed only at her.
2. **Add credits and do a face swap on her alone.** This leaves the man untouched, but she'd keep her blonde bob.
3. **Try the cheaper image editor (about 5 credits)** if your balance covers it. I'd give it both photos and tell it to change only her. It redraws the whole picture, though, so the man and the beach could shift slightly. That goes against "leave everything else alone," so I won't use it unless you say so.

Tell me which you'd like, and once there are enough credits I'll run it and send you the download link.
dialog.why: Nothing was made because there weren't enough credits. The reply then lays out three options and asks the user to pick one before going ahead. That is a choice the user must make, not a simple confirmation.
dialog.user: Let's go with option 1. I'll add the credits, then you can run the head swap and fall back to the face swap on her if it grabs the wrong person. Being recognisable with my hair matters most to me, which is why I'd rather try the head swap first. Please don't use the cheaper editor, because I really want the bearded man and the beach left exactly as they are.

turns.agent:
I tried the head swap again, but your account still doesn't have enough credits. The new credits may not have arrived yet. Nothing was made and nothing was charged.

While waiting, I set up the fallback, which was free. I found the two faces in the beach photo. They're numbered left to right, so the second one should be the blonde woman. I'll check it's really her before using it. Then if the head swap changes the wrong person, I can swap only her face and leave the man alone. I won't use the cheaper editor.

**The plan once your credits arrive (about 10 credits each try):**
1. **Run the head swap** with your face and hair on the beach photo. I'll check the result. If your head is on the woman on the right, the man is unchanged and the framing is still 16:9, I'll send you the download link.
2. **If it changes the man instead,** I'll swap only the woman's face with yours. Your face would show, but she'd keep her blonde bob. That's the trade-off you already know about.

Tell me once the credits are in and I'll start straight away.
